key_insight: A large pretrained video prediction model (Cosmos-Predict2) can be adapted directly into a visuomotor policy with minimal changes, leveraging its learned spatiotemporal priors to produce effective control and planning without complex multi-stage retraining or new action-generation modules.
problem_solved: Reduces the complexity and engineering overhead of converting powerful video generation models into robot control policies by avoiding multi-stage post-training and heavy architectural additions while retaining strong temporal and physical reasoning.
method: Single-stage fine-tuning of a pretrained video model (Cosmos-Predict2) to map observations to actions, preserving spatiotemporal priors learned from large-scale video.
Introduce lightweight action-conditioning (e.g., action tokens or small decoder head) and train end-to-end on control data instead of adding complex new modules.
Use the model's generative rollouts for short-horizon planning or sample-based action selection at inference to guide visuomotor behavior.
impact: Makes it practical for ML and robotics teams to reuse state-of-the-art video models for control and planning, lowering implementation cost and accelerating progress on embodied tasks that require temporal understanding.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: pretrained video model → lightweight action head → policy output (showing minimal added components).
Before/After schematic: multi-stage complex adaptation vs. Cosmos Policy single-stage fine-tune.
Rollout visualization: predicted future frames with corresponding planned actions over time.
Bar/line chart: conceptual comparison of development complexity and sample efficiency versus prior multi-stage methods.
paper_title: Cosmos Policy: Fine-Tuning Video Models for Visuomotor Control and Planning
paper_authors: Moo Jin Kim, Yihuai Gao, Tsung-Yi Lin, Yen-Chen Lin, Yunhao Ge
